summary: Introductory partner discovery call. Apogee is a GPU/cloud vendor exploring go-to-market and technical integration with Redwood; initial fit looks promising around joint benchmarking, reference architecture for private/dedicated deployments, and partner referral agreement. Key concerns: SOC2, network isolation/VPC peering, KMS support, and predictable latency for large context models.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, Jordan from Redwood here, thanks for taking the time. happy holidays as well. quick roll call?
[00:08] Marcus Vela: Marcus here, CTO at Apogee.
[00:12] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, partnerships.
[00:15] Liam Chen: Liam, infra eng.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: Priya on the Redwood infra team, hi all.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: cool, agenda is quick intros, high-level partner thesis, then dig into tech and ops constraints, and next steps. is that good?
[00:30] Marcus Vela: yep sounds good.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: great. so Apogee, do you want to kick off with how you think about partnerships and where you see Redwood fitting in?
[00:44] Sofia Ruiz: yeah, sure. we've been talking to a handful of inference platforms. Apogee sells GPU clouds and racks to SaaS and enterprise, and we get asked for turnkey LLM serving setups. we see two lanes; marketplace/referral where we point customers to a hosted provider, and deeper infra integrations for white-labeled or co-managed stacks.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: makes sense, thanks. our partner angle is similar -- we can be a hosted API for customers or run in dedicated pools on top of partner infra or in a private VPC/on-prem. common playbooks are: 1) Redwood hosted + partner referral for new customers, 2) Dedicated capacity that runs on partner's GPU pools with our orchestration, 3) Private deployments for regulated customers.
[01:29] Marcus Vela: ok the dedicated option is interesting — basically we provide the hardware and networking, you provide runtime, is that right?
[01:37] Priya Natarajan: yeah exactly. the runtime is our GPU-optimized inference engine: kernel selection, batching, KV cache, quantization profiles, that sort of thing. we handle model versions, rollouts, and can integrate with partner autoscaling.
[01:51] Liam Chen: curious about connectivity. for dedicated/dedicated-private, do you need VPC peering or VPN, and what about control plane traffic? we have customers who need air-gapped or strict egress rules.
[02:05] Priya Natarajan: we support a private control plane and there are on-prem options for air-gapped deployments. in VPC setups we typically do peering or transit gateway, and control plane can be customer-managed in private deployments. we also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[02:22] Marcus Vela: and auditing? SOC2, iso? we get asked a lot.
[02:27] Jordan Lee: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we have a compliance package, audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML. we can share the security pack + pen test summary.
[02:36] Sofia Ruiz: great. on the GTM side, we want to know if there is co-marketing or referral margin, and what the sales motion looks like.
[02:44] Jordan Lee: typically we do a referral fee and joint case studies if there are pilot customers. for larger deals we support sales-assisted motions and dedicated account coordination.
[02:52] Marcus Vela: technical Qs: latency guarantees — can you hit p50/p95 targets for long-context models? a lot of our customers push 32k tokens and the cost concerns are big.
[03:06] Priya Natarajan: performance depends on model and quantization; with our runtime and smart routing we target predictable latencies. for long-context models we use kernel optimizations and KV caching; Dedicated gives you most control. we can run benchmark tests on Apogee hardware to produce p50/p95 numbers.
[03:24] Liam Chen: what's the overhead for continuous batching? does it add tail latency?
[03:29] Priya Natarajan: we do workload-aware batching, so there's a tradeoff knob. you can enforce strict latency SLOs which reduces batching efficiency. we can tune batching policy per-sku or per-route.
[03:41] Jordan Lee: on the commercial side, partners often ask about unit economics — can we share quantization recommendations and expected cost/tokens?
[03:49] Priya Natarajan: yes — Redwood Optimize gives recommendations: quantization profiles, caching, and batching settings to hit cost targets while preserving quality. we'll share a sample recommendation report.
[03:59] Marcus Vela: good. on integration, we have an ops portal and an API gateway; do you have terraform or IaC modules for deploying the dedicated stacks?
[04:10] Jordan Lee: we have IaC templates and deployment guides; SEs usually walk partners through the terraform modules and network configs.
[04:18] Sofia Ruiz: any hard limits on model sizes or GPU types? we run mixture of A100s and newer (Xenon-4?), sorry those names blurred.
[04:27] Priya Natarajan: we support a wide catalog; kernel selection is model/hw-aware. sometimes new hw needs a driver/kernel tuning schedule. we'll coordinate for specific SKUs.
[04:36] Marcus Vela: customers ask about data residency and log retention — can retention be set per-customer?
[04:42] Jordan Lee: yes retention and audit log retention are configurable; for Private deployments data stays on-prem.
[04:48] Liam Chen: what's the onboarding time for a dedicated pool on partner infra — weeks? months?
[04:53] Priya Natarajan: typical pilot is 2-6 weeks depending on access and benchmarks; production onboarding for bigger customers can be 6-12 weeks.
[05:02] Jordan Lee: shall we talk about a concrete pilot? Marcus, do you have a reference customer/profile we could use for a benchmark?
[05:09] Marcus Vela: yes we have a SaaS search customer doing reranking and chat with a 16k context. they care about p95 < 800ms for simple rerank and cost less than X per 1M tokens — we'll share numbers.
[05:24] Priya Natarajan: perfect — we can do two tracks: 1) functional POC to validate correctness/quality (small dataset), 2) performance run on Apogee hardware for latency/cost numbers.
[05:36] Sofia Ruiz: legal side — we usually require an MSA and a partner addendum for revenue share. NDA sometimes as well.
[05:43] Jordan Lee: yep we can loop in legal; will introduce legal contacts once both sides agree.
[05:49] Marcus Vela: competitors — we've talked to Lambda Labs and PinnacleAI; their pricing is different and some offer vertically-integrated stacks. how is Redwood differentiated?
[05:59] Jordan Lee: our differentiation is production-first runtime and unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private, plus tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs and observability. we focus on helping partners move customers to production quickly.
[06:12] Liam Chen: a few nitty-grittys: what telemetry do you need onboarded? can we route traces to our existing observability stack?
[06:20] Priya Natarajan: yes we emit traces and logs, and can plug into partner tracing backends. we can also forward metrics to the partner prometheus/observability endpoints if needed.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: ok i want to call out a few risks — driver/stack incompatibilities for bleeding-edge GPUs, and long lead times for certain firmware patches. we handle a lot of this in the onboarding checklist but partners should expect some coordination.
[06:46] Marcus Vela: understood. from a business model perspective, what does Redwood expect from a partner? exclusivity? sales motions?
[06:53] Sofia Ruiz: yes curious about tiers.
[06:55] Jordan Lee: we typically do non-exclusive partnerships. we offer referral margins, and for strategic partners there's a co-sell program with deal registration and higher margin splits.
[07:05] Marcus Vela: great. next steps for us — we'll pull sample workload definitions and access to a staging cluster, and you'll share partner docs and pricing.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: action items noted. i'll share the partner one-pager and pricing. Priya will share benchmark template and sample IaC.
[07:23] Priya Natarajan: i'll also include a short security pack (SOC2 cert and SAML integration guide).
[07:29] Sofia Ruiz: ok timing — can we aim to have docs and template by Thursday? (2026-12-23)
[07:36] Jordan Lee: yes that's doable.
[07:39] Marcus Vela: we'll collate sample workloads and get them over.
[07:42] Jordan Lee: perfect. any other questions?
[07:45] Liam Chen: none from me.
[07:47] Sofia Ruiz: all good.
[07:49] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email recapping next steps. happy holidays.
[07:55] Marcus Vela: thanks. bye.
[08:00] <auto-generated summary> Intro call focused on partner integration models (referral, dedicated, private), technical requirements (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2), and pilot plan (functional POC + performance benchmark). Next steps assigned.
